data.cultural_impact: The name Shuwair holds a unique cultural significance in Arabic tradition. The name can be associated with tranquility, peace, and relaxation, much like a calm night. In many Middle Eastern cultures, the night is seen as a time of rest and reflection, and the name Shuwair reflects the serene and soothing aspects of the night.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Shuwair is believed to represent the inner peace and strength that comes from overcoming hardships. In Islamic tradition, the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is said to have identified strength and endurance as essential qualities for followers of his faith. The name Shuwair serves as a reminder of the importance of resilience and patience in the face of adversity, and the deeper spiritual significance of this name is thus deeply rooted in the Islamic faith.

historical_references.context: Battle of Uhud: Shuwair ibn Sakhr led the Arabian polytheists against the Muslim army, using a force of 3,000 men. He was defeated and, according to Muslim tradition, this was due to the intervention of the angel Gabriel in the battle.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Baladhuri, Ansab al-Ashraf, p. 435 The name Shuwair carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The Second Fitna: Al-Aswad ibn Muqrin, a member of the Banu Asad tribe, was a rebel leader during the Second Fitna (civil war). He was known as Shuwair ibn Al-Hakim. He was captured and executed by 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, the fourth caliph.
